slides.texte_overlay:
How to leave a strong first
impression in five minutes
Minute one: smile before you speak. A warm face tells people you're friendly before you've said a single word, and it relaxes both of you.
Minute two: ask one curious question. "What brought you here tonight?" Open questions get people talking about what matters to them.
Minute three: share one small, real detail about yourself. A hobby, a funny moment from your week. A little openness makes you human and memorable.
Minute four: find something you have in common. A city, a sport, a favourite food. Shared ground turns a stranger into someone familiar.
Minute five: bring a little spark. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a fun fact is often what people remember about me later.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A fun fact is often what people remember about me later.

slides.texte_overlay: Throughout: keep your phone away and your eyes on them. Full attention for five minutes is rarer and more impressive than any clever line.
Last: end warmly and use their name. "Really nice meeting you, David." People remember how you made them feel in the last seconds.
